Estimate an EBIC graphical lasso network

Source: R/build_aliases.R
build_glasso.Rd

build_network(method = "glasso"), or for short build_glasso(), estimates an EBIC graphical lasso network, a Gaussian graphical model, from numeric variables. The edge between two variables is their partial correlation given all the others, shrunk by the graphical lasso, with the penalty chosen by EBIC (Friedman et al., 2008; Foygel & Drton, 2010).

The penalty is chosen along a path of nlambda values; an L1 penalty sets small partial correlations to exactly zero. An absent edge means the penalty removed it at the selected lambda, not that the two variables are shown to be independent. Check the stability of the edges and centralities with boot_glasso().

Usage

build_glasso(
  data,
  actor = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  ...,
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 100L,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall"),
  predictability = TRUE,
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  params = list()
)

Arguments

data

The variables: a data frame with one row per observation and one column per variable, or a square symmetric correlation or covariance matrix, which needs the sample size in params (as in params = list(n = 250)). Non-numeric columns are set aside; a frame of two or more character or factor columns and fewer than two numeric ones is read as sequences and turned into per-row state counts first. A column named rid is set aside; columns with non-syntactic names, all-missing and constant columns, and rows with a missing value are dropped, each with a message; fewer than 2 variables or 3 complete rows raise an error.

actor

The id column naming whose observation each row is (a person). With level, the decomposition groups by it; without, it is set aside, not modelled. Default NULL.

level

Multilevel decomposition, with actor: "between" estimates the network of person means, "within" the network of deviations from them, and "both" returns the two as a netobject_ml. Default NULL (no decomposition).

...

Further arguments for build_network(). method cannot be given (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

gamma

The EBIC hyperparameter: larger values give sparser networks. Default 0.5.

nlambda

The number of penalties tried. Default 100.

cor_method

"pearson" (default), "spearman" or "kendall", passed to stats::cor().

predictability

Whether to compute each node's predictability (the R-squared of the node on its neighbours). It is stored on the network, and cograph::splot() draws it as a ring around each node. Default TRUE.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata (covariates), never read as variables. Default NULL.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

params

Settings for the estimator, as a named list: lambda.min.ratio (default 0.01), penalize.diagonal (default FALSE), refit (default FALSE; TRUE re-estimates the selected edges without the penalty), and n, the sample size when data is a correlation or covariance matrix. The network stores them, so the resampling verbs re-estimate with the same settings. Default list().

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group, a netobject_ml with level = "both"), as build_network() returns it.

References

Friedman, J., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics, 9(3), 432–441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604–612.

See also

build_network() for every method; build_pcor() for the unregularised network; boot_glasso() and nct() for inference.

Examples

build_network(srl_strategies, method = "glasso")
#> Partial Correlation Network (EBICglasso) [undirected]
#>   Sample size: 250
#>   Weights: [0.020, 0.325]  |  +13 / -0 edges
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (10 of 13):
#>    from         to           weight
#>    Time_Mgmt    Effort_Reg   0.325 
#>    Monitoring   Evaluating   0.300 
#>    Elaboration  Organization 0.262 
#>    Planning     Monitoring   0.229 
#>    Elaboration  Rehearsal    0.158 
#>    Evaluating   Organization 0.154 
#>    Organization Rehearsal    0.152 
#>    Planning     Time_Mgmt    0.130 
#>    Planning     Evaluating   0.130 
#>    Evaluating   Effort_Reg   0.093  
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix.
#> 
#>   Predictability (R²):
#>   Monitoring    0.173  ████████████████████████████████████████
#>   Evaluating    0.173  ████████████████████████████████████████
#>   Organization  0.137  ████████████████████████████████
#>   Time_Mgmt     0.133  ███████████████████████████████
#>   Effort_Reg    0.122  ████████████████████████████
#>   Planning      0.119  ████████████████████████████
#>   Elaboration   0.115  ██████████████████████████
#>   Rehearsal     0.067  ███████████████
#>   Help_Seeking  0.006  █
#> 
#>   Gamma: 0.50  |  Lambda: 0.1319
